references.text: The Harvest Festival is mentioned in connection with gathering the crop from the field, which corresponds to the collection of the land's produce in the seventh month.
The Feast of Tabernacles at the turn of the year, when the harvest is completed, corresponds to the celebration after the gathering of the crops.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month there shall be a holy assembly with a seven-day festival for the Lord.
The Feast of Tabernacles shall be celebrated for seven days after the grain and wine have been gathered in, with joy before the Lord.
The Israelites celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days after returning from exile, as prescribed.
The Jewish Feast of Tabernacles is mentioned as the background for Jesus' journey to Jerusalem.
On the last, great day of the feast (the eighth day), Jesus spoke about living water, which relates to the Sabbath rest on the eighth day.
